# opencode-venice-balance

> An OpenCode TUI plugin for displaying your Venice.ai balance

## Prerequisites

- OpenCode v2
- Venice.ai account with an Admin API key
- Environment variable: `VENICE_ADMIN_API_KEY`

**Note:** This plugin requires an Admin API key, not a regular API key. Admin
keys have access to billing endpoints that regular keys cannot access. You can
generate an Admin API key from your Venice.ai account settings.

## Installation

The one-step path, which installs the package and registers it in your global
OpenCode configuration:

```bash
opencode plugin add @jcyamo/opencode-venice-balance
```

OpenCode loads the plugin's `./tui` entrypoint automatically once the package is
listed, so there is nothing to register separately.

### Registering manually

Install the package:

```bash
pnpm add @jcyamo/opencode-venice-balance
# or: npm install @jcyamo/opencode-venice-balance
```

Then add it to `plugins` in your global `opencode.jsonc`:

```jsonc
{
	"plugins": ["@jcyamo/opencode-venice-balance"],
}
```

A TUI-only plugin can also live in `cli.json`, which keeps it active when the
CLI is connected to a remote server:

```jsonc
// ~/.config/opencode/cli.json
{
	"plugins": ["@jcyamo/opencode-venice-balance"],
}
```

### From a local checkout

The plugin is loaded from a built package, so build it first, then register the
absolute path with an npm `file:` specifier in `cli.json`:

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm build
```

```jsonc
// ~/.config/opencode/cli.json
{
	"plugins": [
		"@jcyamo/opencode-venice-balance@file:/absolute/path/to/opencode-venice-balance",
	],
}
```

OpenCode copies the package into its cache when it loads it. After changing the
source, rebuild and restart the CLI for the new build to take effect. Use
`pnpm build:watch` while iterating.

### Setting the environment variable

Add to your shell configuration (e.g., `~/.bashrc`, `~/.zshrc`):

```bash
export VENICE_ADMIN_API_KEY="your-admin-api-key-here"
```

Or set it inline when running OpenCode:

```bash
VENICE_ADMIN_API_KEY="your-key" opencode
```

## Features

- **Real-time DIEM Balance** - Displays your current DIEM balance and percentage
  of epoch allocation remaining
- **Visual Status Indicators** - Color-coded indicators for balance status (low,
  exhausted, using USD fallback)
- **Automatic Updates** - Balance refreshes automatically during your OpenCode
  session
- **Manual Refresh** - Press `<leader>v` to manually refresh your balance
- **Error Handling** - User-friendly error messages with actionable solutions

The balance is shown in the session sidebar. If the sidebar is hidden, open it
with `<leader>b` (`session.sidebar` in `cli.json` controls the default).

## Keybinding

| Key         | Action          |
| ----------- | --------------- |
| `<leader>v` | Refresh balance |

## Error States

| Error          | Display                       | Cause                                  | Solution                                                                                    |
| -------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `no_key`       | "Set VENICE_ADMIN_API_KEY"    | Environment variable not set           | Set `VENICE_ADMIN_API_KEY` in your shell configuration or export it before running OpenCode |
| `invalid_key`  | "invalid or not an Admin key" | API key is invalid or is a regular key | Verify your key is an Admin API key from your Venice.ai account settings                    |
| `fetch_failed` | "Failed to fetch"             | Network error or API unavailable       | Check your internet connection and try again; the Venice.ai API may be temporarily down     |
| `not_staking`  | "Not staking DIEM"            | Account is not currently staking DIEM  | Enable staking in your Venice.ai account to earn DIEM allocations                           |
| `exhausted`    | "Exhausted"                   | DIEM balance fully consumed            | Your DIEM allocation is depleted; wait for the next epoch or add funds                      |
| `usd_fallback` | "Using USD reserve"           | DIEM exhausted, using USD balance      | Add more DIEM to your staking balance or the account will consume from USD reserve          |

## Troubleshooting

### Balance not showing

1. Verify `VENICE_ADMIN_API_KEY` is set: `echo $VENICE_ADMIN_API_KEY`
2. Ensure you're using an Admin API key, not a regular API key
3. Confirm the plugin loaded: `opencode plugin list`, or check
   `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log` for a `jcyamo.venice-balance`
   entry
4. Make sure the session sidebar is open (`<leader>b`)
5. Try refreshing manually with `<leader>v`

### Shows "Not staking"

Your Venice.ai account does not have an active staking position. To stake DIEM:

1. Log into your Venice.ai account
2. Navigate to the staking section
3. Stake tokens to receive DIEM allocations

### Shows incorrect value

1. The balance reflects your current DIEM allocation, not total balance
2. Balance updates periodically; use `<leader>v` to force refresh
3. If persistent, verify your API key has access to billing endpoints

## Development

| Command            | Purpose                     |
| ------------------ | --------------------------- |
| `pnpm build`       | Compile `src/` to `dist/`   |
| `pnpm build:watch` | Recompile on change         |
| `pnpm typecheck`   | Type-check without emitting |
| `pnpm test`        | Run the test suite          |
| `pnpm lint`        | Lint `src/`                 |

The TUI entrypoint is `src/tui.tsx` (exported as `./tui`); `src/index.ts` is a
no-op server entrypoint that exists so the package resolves when listed in
`opencode.jsonc`.

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to
[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [0.2.0] - 2026-09-25

### Changed

- **Breaking:** the plugin targets the OpenCode v2 plugin API
  (`@opencode/plugin/tui`) and no longer loads on OpenCode v1. Users on v1
  should stay on 0.1.x.
- Registration moved from `tui.jsonc` to `opencode.jsonc` or `cli.json`;
  `tui.jsonc` no longer exists in v2.
- `@opencode/theme` is now a development dependency. It is the peer that carries
  `ResolvedTheme`, and without it installed the theme types degrade to `any` and
  silently defeat token checking.

### Added

- A no-op server entrypoint plus the `"."` package export, so the package
  resolves when it is listed in `opencode.jsonc`.
- `pnpm build:watch` for a tighter local iteration loop.

### Fixed

- The session sidebar crashed on every resolved balance. The palette returned
  resolved theme colors and the view invoked them as functions; the palette is
  now a plain function with unit coverage.

## [0.1.1] - 2026-07-29

### Added

- Documented the one-step `opencode plugin --global` install.

### Fixed

- Overwrite a stale KV error field with an explicit `error: null` on success.

## [0.1.0] - 2026-07-23

### Added

- Initial release. DIEM balance in the OpenCode session sidebar, refreshed on a
  heartbeat and on `<leader>v`.
